title: Envoy filter order is now the same on every listener — EnvoyFilter patches inserted by position may land elsewhere

detection.reason: filter order is decided inside Envoy; the projection carries only which operation an EnvoyFilter uses, not where the resulting chain puts it

quote: The ordering is now consistent across inbound, outbound and gateway proxy modes, as well as HTTP and TCP protocols
remediation: Only EnvoyFilter resources that insert relative to another filter (INSERT_BEFORE / INSERT_AFTER / INSERT_FIRST) can be affected: inbound TCP now places Metadata Exchange before Authn, and gateway TCP places stats after Authz and CUSTOM authz before Authn. Re-check where each positional patch lands with `istioctl proxy-config listener` after upgrading a canary proxy.
verifyCommand: kubectl get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.configPatches[]?.patch.operation] | any(test("^INSERT_(BEFORE|AFTER|FIRST)$"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed EnvoyFilter inserts by position and must be re-checked against the unified filter order

title: The sidecar now ships a startupProbe — pods whose sidecar does not start within 10 minutes are terminated, and hand-tuned readiness values need re-tuning

detection.reason: the sidecar's probe timing is rendered at injection time from Helm values and per-pod annotations; the projection keeps the annotation KEY, not the timing it sets

quote: If the startup probe does not pass after 10 minutes, the pod will be terminated. Previously, the pod would never be terminated even if it was unable to start indefinitely.
remediation: Pods that override the sidecar readiness timing (`readiness.status.sidecar.istio.io/*` annotations or `global.proxy.readiness*` values) were tuned for the old polling; move them to the new defaults (initialDelay 0 / period 15 / failureThreshold 4 with the startup probe on) or set `global.proxy.startupProbe.enabled=false` together with the old readiness values, as the note lists.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations // {} | keys[] | startswith("readiness.status.sidecar.istio.io/")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed pod overrides sidecar readiness timing and was tuned for the pre-startupProbe defaults

title: The in-cluster operator can no longer install the ambient profile

detection.reason: IstioOperator resources are not collected; only the operator's own Deployment and the CRD are visible

quote: **Removed** support for installing `ambient` profile with in-cluster operator.
remediation: An `IstioOperator` resource with `spec.profile: ambient` that is reconciled by the in-cluster operator stops installing at 1.20. Move the ambient install to `istioctl install` or the Helm charts (istio-cni, ztunnel, istiod with `profile=ambient`); the in-cluster operator itself is deprecated.
verifyCommand: kubectl get istiooperators.install.istio.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.profile == "ambient") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed IstioOperator asks the in-cluster operator for the ambient profile, which 1.20 no longer installs

title: `PILOT_ENABLE_DESTINATION_RULE_INHERITANCE` is removed — DestinationRule inheritance stops working if it was turned on

detection.reason: checked on the istiod Deployment's container env NAMES only — a flag set through `pilot.env` in a values file lands there; one set via `meshConfig` or an IstioOperator that has not been applied yet is not scanned

quote: **Removed** the `PILOT_ENABLE_DESTINATION_RULE_INHERITANCE` experimental feature, which has been disable-by-default since it was created.
remediation: Remove the variable from istiod. If it was set to `true`, mesh-wide or namespace-wide DestinationRules no longer merge into host-specific ones — copy the inherited `trafficPolicy` settings into each host DestinationRule before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_ENABLE_DESTINATION_RULE_INHERITANCE)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # a printed line is the removed flag; a value of true means inherited DestinationRule settings are lost at 1.20

title: The `forward_downstream_sni`, `tcp_cluster_rewrite` and `sni_verifier` network filters are no longer in the Envoy build

detection.reason: checked on the filter names an EnvoyFilter references in its match and in the top-level `name` of its patch value — a filter named deeper inside a typed_config is not scanned

quote: **Removed** `forward_downstream_sni`, `tcp_cluster_rewrite`, and `sni_verifier` custom Istio network filters from Envoy build. This functionality can be achieved using the Wasm extensibility.
remediation: An EnvoyFilter that adds or matches one of these three filters is rejected by the 1.20 proxy (the listener fails to load). Replace the behaviour with a Wasm extension (WasmPlugin) or drop the patch before upgrading the data plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(tojson | test("forward_downstream_sni|tcp_cluster_rewrite|sni_verifier")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed EnvoyFilter references a network filter the 1.20 Envoy build no longer has
